title: The Cold Start
primary_metric: recommendations clicked (specifically, on the premiere series) per 100 accounts that started signup -- not per account that completed it

options.A: The Popularity Path -- ship every new account straight to a recommendation shelf built from a small item-similarity matrix seeded only by aggregate popularity, in which the premiere's own row and column are still completely empty
options.B: The Ratings Gate -- withhold any recommendation shelf until the new account rates 10 titles and builds a real, if sparse, row of the user-item ratings matrix that can actually match the premiere's genre

Used as a real historical floor for MA3, not as the modeled 2026 value directly -- the population (2002 self-selected MovieLens research-community members) is a dated, different-context proxy for a 2026 friend-referral streaming cohort.

Option B -- The Ratings Gate (User-Item Ratings Matrix)
Primary Metric -- Recommendations Clicked per 100 Accounts That Started Signup

balance.argument_a: Zero onboarding friction means literally all 100 starters reach a recommendation shelf -- nobody is lost to the flow itself. A real precedent shows even a much shorter, lower-friction, already-purchase-intent flow (e-commerce checkout) already loses 17% of users to complexity alone (S4); adding a 10-item rating requirement before a first-time visitor has even decided whether they like the app risks losing meaningfully more. Yes, the premiere's own row and column in the similarity matrix are completely empty on day one -- but under the modeled 20% click-through rate (MA2), a real fraction of all 100 starters still click it, and nobody is turned away at the door to do so.
balance.argument_b: Its personalization is real, not decorative: once an account clears the gate, its own sparse row (10 filled cells) gives the system actual signal to match genre-relevant content, converting at a modeled 35% among completers (MA4) -- nearly double the Popularity Path's modeled 20% (MA2). The required-ratings mechanic is not invented for this case: it is the literal onboarding design the real MovieLens research platform used, live, with real users (S2). That same precedent also measured real abandonment -- 13.96% of a patient, already-engaged 2002 research population dropped before finishing (S2) -- and a modern, mobile-first, friend-referral cohort in 2026 is modeled as dropping out even more (MA3), not less, which is exactly the cost the per-100-starters metric is designed to charge against B.
balance.margin_basis: Compute clicks per 100 starters for both options (Appendix D): Option A = 100 starters x MA2's 20% CTR. Option B = (100 starters x (1 - MA3's modeled 40% dropout)) x MA4's 35% completer CTR. Compare.
balance.margin_note: COMPUTED 2026-09-01 (case-research). PASS 1 (literal historical figure, S2's real 13.96% dropout, completion 86.04%): Option A = 100 x 0.20 = 20.0 clicks/100. Option B = 86.04 x 0.35 = 30.11 clicks/100. margin = (30.11-20.0)/30.11 x 100 = 33.6% -- OVER SPEC §2's ~20% cap. RETUNE (per SPEC §2's own instruction to adjust a constraint, not hide data): S2's 13.96% figure is a real number but from a dated (2002), self-selected, already-engaged research-community population, not a general 2026 friend-referral streaming cohort -- a materially different population is a legitimate constraint to retune, anchored above two real cited figures (S2's own 13.96% floor and S4's real 17% checkout-complexity floor from a shorter, lower-friction flow). Retuned to MA3 = 40% modeled 2026 dropout (completion 60.0). PASS 2 (retuned): Option A = 100 x 0.20 = 20.0 clicks/100. Option B = 60.0 x 0.35 = 21.0 clicks/100. margin = (21.0-20.0)/21.0 x 100 = 4.76%. WINNER: Option B, The Ratings Gate, by a genuinely close margin. Additional sensitivity checked: at MA2 (CTR_A) = 12% instead of 20% (a stricter 'more buried' reading), clicks_A = 12.0, margin widens to (21.0-12.0)/21.0 = 42.9% -- confirms MA2 is also a real driver of how close this case reads, alongside MA3. Full trail also in RESEARCH_LOG.md.

modeling_assumptions.claim: Days from case launch to Priya's launch review
modeling_assumptions.basis: Matches the Overview's Thursday-review, Friday-premiere framing.

modeling_assumptions.claim: Click-through rate on the premiere recommendation among all accounts that reach the Popularity Path's shelf
modeling_assumptions.basis: No platform publishes click-through data for a same-week premiere appearing in an unpersonalized shelf. A modest but non-zero value, reflecting organic exposure surviving a heavily marketed premiere week even without personalization.
modeling_assumptions.sensitivity: HIGH -- the most narratively-invented number in the case; margin widens to 42.9% if this drops to 12% (see balance.margin_note).

modeling_assumptions.claim: Modeled onboarding dropout during the Ratings Gate, Northline's 2026 mobile-first, friend-referral cohort
modeling_assumptions.basis: Anchored above two real, cited figures: Baymard's real, confirmed 17% cart/checkout abandonment (S4, a shorter, lower-friction, already-purchase-intent flow) and the real, historically measured 13.96% dropout on an identical rate->=10-titles gate on the real 2002 MovieLens site (S2, a self-selected, already-engaged research-community population, not a general new-subscriber cohort).
modeling_assumptions.sensitivity: HIGH -- the single most dilemma-relevant modeling choice in the case; using the literal S2 figure (13.96%) instead pushes margin_pct to 33.6%, over SPEC §2's ~20% cap. See balance.margin_note.

modeling_assumptions.claim: Click-through rate on the premiere recommendation among accounts that complete the Ratings Gate
modeling_assumptions.basis: Only some fraction of an account's 10 ratings will happen to land in the premiere's own genre; not independently sourced, since no platform publishes click-through data for an unreleased show.
modeling_assumptions.sensitivity: MEDIUM -- see RESEARCH_LOG.md for margin recomputed at alternate values.

modeling_assumptions.claim: Appendix E's worked-example matrices (P, U, and the target blend)
modeling_assumptions.basis: Illustrative scenario numbers, scaled down for a clean hand-worked example.
modeling_assumptions.sensitivity: None -- pedagogical only; does not feed the primary metric in Appendix D.

sensitivity_note: margin_pct (4.76%) is computed entirely from four stated Modeling Assumptions (MA2, MA3, MA4, plus the fixed 100-account cohort) -- none of Appendix D's numbers are directly measured Northline data, since Northline is fictional. MA3 (modeled 2026 dropout) is the single most load-bearing choice: recomputing with S2's literal real 2002 dropout figure (13.96%) instead pushes the margin to 33.6%, over SPEC §2's cap, with Option B winning by a wide margin instead of a close one. MA2 (Option A's CTR) is the second most sensitive: dropping it from 20% to 12% widens the margin to 42.9%. See balance.margin_note and sensitivity_model.py.

cohort_bands.note: The size the case was authored for. Socratic plan and Anchor timings run as written (45 minutes, all 4 anchors, full twist, threaded deep conflict).

Anchors 2-3 combine into one pass; the twist still drops at the same relative point but only one deep-conflict thread runs (recommend the metric-integrity thread, since it has the sharpest numeric payoff once Appendix D is worked through); total runtime shortens to roughly 30 minutes, content held constant.

No vote to take at Anchor 1 -- the learner states an initial position instead. The facilitator plays devil's advocate directly rather than cold-calling. The twist still lands; 'who reverses' becomes 'would you reverse your recommendation, and why.'

MA3 (modeled onboarding dropout, 40%) is explicitly flagged HIGH/'the single most dilemma-relevant modeling choice in the case' in case.md -- anchored above two real cited figures (Baymard 17%, MovieLens 2002 13.96%) but the 2026-cohort transfer value is a stated scenario choice, not a direct citation.
Derived from the same MA2 framing (completer engagement rate) -- no platform publishes this figure for a fictional service; irreducible scenario estimate, same basis as MA2's HIGH-sensitivity flag.
